- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >90), model tends to overshoot and then sharply correct — overpredicting the peak and failing to capture subsequent mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends (e.g., 80–85 range) — fails to recognize support levels or downward momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts show exaggerated swings that don’t match true price behavior.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of mean reversion — prices often return to prior levels faster than forecasted.
- Model fails to capture the “tail” of price corrections — often underestimates how quickly prices fall after a peak.
- Model overestimates the persistence of recent trends — fails to recognize that price momentum often reverses within 10–15 days.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market events — tends to ignore structural shifts (e.g., auction rules, compliance deadlines) in short-term forecasts.
- Model shows bias toward higher prices in the final 5–10 days — often overestimates the “end-of-horizon” price, especially in downward trends.
